===== NEW MESSAGES SINCE YOUR LAST DECISION =====

**Coordinator (Claude) — decision after round 1**

Looking at round 1, this isn't really a fight — it's the same asymmetry the project saw in ios_architecture_review: the fallback Codex seat (local Qwen standing in for gpt-5.3-codex-spark) gave a generic, correct-but-shallow pass (SwiftData is good, batch-fetch, snapshot the queue, watch permissions, think about StoreKit later — plus a bare-bones `Deck`/`Card`/`DueQueryService`/`SessionEngine` sketch), while Claude put a full, specific tech-spec draft on the table that goes well beyond restating prior decisions.

The substantive new material Codex hasn't had a chance to react to yet:
- A third data model, `ReviewLogEntry`, separate from `Card` — because `Card` only knows its *current* schedule, and the daily-history chart, retention rate, and per-deck attribution in mixed sessions all need a durable log of every past grading event, not just present state.
- A more specific CloudKit-shape rule than "no `.unique`": every non-optional attribute needs a default, every relationship must be Optional.
- A `DebugClockOverride` (DEBUG-only launch argument) that turns the long-standing "advance the simulator clock and relaunch" manual check into a real, automated `XCUITest` — proving the *app-level* due-computation wiring, not just the pure SM-2 module.
- A previously-unnamed edge case: a device clock moving *backward* shouldn't be able to make an already-graded-today card look due again — needs its own `TestClock` unit test.
- An explicit lock request: cards belong permanently to the deck they were created in, no move-between-decks feature, since the denormalized `isDemo`/`deckID` fields on `Card`/`ReviewLogEntry` depend on that being true.
- A concrete file/module layout and a three-tier test strategy (`RecallCoreTests`, `RecallAppTests` with in-memory `ModelContainer`, `RecallAppUITests`).

None of this contradicts anything Codex said — it's a superset again — but Codex's message doesn't engage with any of it specifically, so I don't think it's honest to call this converged after one round, same as the last phase.

CONSENSUS: NO

Next round needs Codex to respond directly to Claude's specific proposals — the `ReviewLogEntry` model and its denormalization, the sharper CloudKit-shape rule (Optional relationships + defaulted attributes), the `DebugClockOverride`/automated day-boundary XCUITest, the backward-clock-jump safety test, the "cards never move between decks" lock, and the proposed file layout/test-tier split — either endorsing them as binding or raising a concrete objection, so this phase locks one coherent spec rather than one detailed draft sitting unchallenged.

**Claude (Frontend Engineer · Visionary) — Round 2**

Okay, so Codex's round 1 message is basically the same generic pass as last phase, but there's one specific thing in it I want to flag hard rather than let slide: the `interfaces-json` Codex submitted defines `Deck` and `Card` as plain `Codable` structs with a `DueQueryService`/`SessionEngine` as protocols returning cards `async`. That's not a stylistic quibble — it directly contradicts what's already locked. `ios_architecture_review` decided grade/demo fields must be raw `Int`/`Bool` on SwiftData models specifically because `#Predicate` can't reliably filter certain types, and the whole batched-fetch requirement (`DEC-design_handoff-006`) assumes `Deck`/`Card` are `@Model` classes living in a `ModelContext`, not value-type structs you'd fetch through an async protocol method. If a build lane actually coded against Codex's version, they'd build a repository-pattern abstraction over SwiftData that this project explicitly doesn't need and that adds exactly the kind of ceremony the architecture review already rejected in favor of MV. So I'm not folding that part in — `Deck` and `Card` stay `@Model` classes as I specified, and I think this needs to be said plainly rather than politely split-the-difference, because there isn't a real difference to split; one of these compiles against SwiftData's actual constraints and one doesn't.

On the substance nobody's actually pushed back on — the `ReviewLogEntry` model, the sharper CloudKit-shape rule, `DebugClockOverride`, the backward-clock test, cards-never-move-between-decks — I'm going to treat the lack of a specific counter-argument the same way the group treated it in `ios_architecture_review`: as the fallback model not having the depth to argue with specifics, not as tacit disagreement. I'll restate why each matters once more, briefly, because I'd rather over-justify than have something get quietly cut. `ReviewLogEntry` is the one I'd fight hardest for if anyone pushed back, because without it there is genuinely no data source for the daily-history chart or retention rate — `Card` is Markovian, it forgets everything except its current state the moment you grade it. If a build lane skips this model because it seems like more schema than the MVP needs, Stats becomes unbuildable as specified and someone will improvise a worse solution under time pressure, like inferring history from `nextReviewDate` deltas, which doesn't actually work.

Here's a bolder thing I want to add this round, and it's genuinely new, not just restating round 1. The design spec already requires VoiceOver to announce "Good, next review in 6 days" — computed live, not a static string — which means we're already committed to being able to compute all four grade outcomes from a card's current schedule before the user taps anything. If we're computing that anyway for accessibility, I think it's a mistake not to surface it visually too: a small `.caption` line under each of the four grade buttons in `ReviewGradeRow` — "1d / 12d / 20d / 26d" or similar, monospaced-digit, quiet enough not to fight the reveal moment for attention — showing what tapping that button will actually do to the schedule before you commit to it. This isn't new decision logic or a new screen, it's exposing a computation the spec already requires, and it's exactly the kind of thing that makes "trust the schedule" a felt experience instead of a slogan you have to take on faith after the fact. I'd add one pure function for this, `SM2Engine.previewOutcomes(current:clock:) -> [Grade: CardSchedule]`, called once per card reveal, feeding both the VoiceOver labels and the button captions from the same source — which also means I don't need a second, UI-specific formatting function drifting out of sync with the real scheduler. If anyone thinks this crowds the review card visually against the "ledger, not clutter" design constraint, I'd push back that four small numbers under four buttons the user is about to look at anyway is not clutter, it's the entire point of a legible ledger — but I'll cop to this being a genuine judgment call and not something I'll die on if the group think it dilutes the flip-reveal moment.

Last thing: I want `Card.deck` to be treated as effectively immutable in application logic — not necessarily a Swift `let` (SwiftData relationships need to be `var` for the framework's own machinery), but there should be no `moveCard(to:)` function anywhere in this interface contract, and I want that absence to be read as intentional, not an oversight, given how much the denormalized `isDemo`/`deckID` fields on `Card` and `ReviewLogEntry` depend on a card's deck membership never changing after creation. If someone genuinely wants a "move card to another deck" feature later, that's new scope requiring the same justification pass everything else beyond the six core features needs — it's not something to slip in as an obvious convenience during build.

## Final Output

**Architecture overview:** `RecallCore` is a real local Swift Package — pure SM-2 engine, shared due-computation, RFC4180 CSV parser/writer — with zero SwiftData/SwiftUI imports and every "now"-dependent call taking an injected `Clock`. The app layer is MV, not MVVM: views hold `@Environment(\.modelContext)` for direct CRUD; review-queue construction and stats aggregation go through two dedicated `@Observable @MainActor` services, `DueQueryService` and `SessionEngine`, so "one shared function" is enforced by there being exactly one type. Three tabs (Decks, Stats, Settings); Review is a `fullScreenCover`, never a tab.

**Data models (SwiftData `@Model` classes, not `Codable` structs):**
- `Deck` — id, name, createdAt, isArchived, isDemo, cascade-deleting `cards` relationship.
- `Card` — id, front, back, note, `deck` relationship, easeFactor, intervalDays, repetitions, nextReviewDate, isDemo (denormalized from deck), lastGradeRaw. Cards belong permanently to their creation deck — no `moveCard` function exists anywhere in this contract, and that absence is intentional.
- `ReviewLogEntry` (new this phase) — id, timestamp, gradeRaw, cardID, deckID, isDemo. `Card` is Markovian and only knows its current state; the daily-history chart, retention rate, and per-deck attribution in mixed sessions all need this durable per-grading-event log.
- All `#Predicate`-filtered fields stay flat `Int`/`Bool`/`Date`/`UUID` — never enums. No `@Attribute(.unique)` anywhere. CloudKit-shape is refined to a concrete rule: every relationship must be Optional, every non-optional attribute must have a default.

**Persistence strategy:** one `ModelContainer` for `[Deck, Card, ReviewLogEntry]`, a `SchemaMigrationPlan` established from day one even at version 1. Every grade write goes through a single `GradeRecorder.record` call site that mutates the card's schedule via `SM2Engine`, inserts a `ReviewLogEntry`, and calls `context.save()` synchronously — atomic, one writer, never two call sites drifting out of sync.

**Testing strategy (three tiers):** `RecallCoreTests` — pure `XCTest`, `TestClock`-driven: first-review, lapse-reset, ease floor under repeated Again, Hard-must-underperform-Good at ease 2.8/interval 20, spring-forward and fall-back DST transitions, and a new backward-clock-jump test (system time rewinding must not make an already-graded-today card look due again), plus RFC4180 edge cases and duplicate detection. `RecallAppTests` — in-memory `ModelContainer` testing `DueQueryService`/`SessionEngine`/`GradeRecorder`/CSV commit against real SwiftData. `RecallAppUITests` — the automated force-quit/relaunch persistence test, plus a new automated day-boundary integration test enabled by `DebugClockOverride`: a `#if DEBUG`-only launch argument (`-RecallClockOffsetDays N`) that swaps in an offset `Clock`, turning the long-standing manual "advance the simulator clock and relaunch" check into a real, fast, CI-runnable `XCUITest` that actually exercises the `DueQueryService` path — compiled entirely out of Release.

**New UI touchpoint:** `SM2Engine.previewOutcomes(current:clock:) -> [Grade: CardSchedule]` computes all four grade outcomes without mutating anything, feeding both the VoiceOver label and a small monospaced-digit caption under each of the four grade buttons in `ReviewGradeRow` showing what tapping it will do to the schedule — one source of truth, no second formatting function to drift out of sync.

**File/module layout:** `RecallApp/` (App entry, `RootTabView`, `Theme/`, `Models/`, `Services/`, `Screens/{Decks,Review,Stats,Settings}`, `Components/`); `RecallCore/` local SPM package with `Sources/RecallCore/` and `Tests/RecallCoreTests/`; `RecallAppTests/`; `RecallAppUITests/`.
